Oh, and Derrick Henry will look to run all over his former team in the Tennessee Titans . That's a must-watch revenge game. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on Tee Higgins at +175 and tight end Harold Fannin Jr . at +235. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 4. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a tight end who looked incredible last week in his 2026 debut. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. 1. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (+160) The Las Vegas Raiders have a massive matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs this week. The Raiders are off to a surprising 3-0 start, although we can't ignore the fact that they've played the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL up to this point, as their first three opponents have won one game combined. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut last week against the New Orleans Saints , and he looked magnificent. He caught a game-high 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in a 35-27 win, and will be important if the Raiders want to score an upset victory over their rivals. With how good Bowers looked last week, I'll sprinkle on him again in this spot as Kirk Cousins ' new clear-cut "WR1." 2. Bills RB James Cook (-140) James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is one of the best running backs in the NFL, and he's on a bit of a heater right now. He rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 vs. the Detroit Lions , and then 24 times for 154 yards and another touchdown last week against the Los Angeles Chargers . Now, the flailing New England Patriots come to town, and they are missing two important defenders in Christian Barmore and Christian Gonzalez . They lost by 29 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, and I'm sure Joe Brady and the Bills want to do something similar to the team that won their division last year. A -140 price isn't value, but I can tell you I was surprised by this listing. 3. Vikings RB Aaron Jones (-160) Like James Cook, this line doesn't offer much value. But consider that the Miami Dolphins have allowed six touchdowns to running backs through three games. The Minnesota Vikings are favored by double-digits over Miami, which makes sense because the Dolphins just lost De'Von Achane for the year, while Brian Flores is going to look to DESTROY his former team from a defensive standpoint. That means Aaron Jones is going to get plenty of touches. He hasn't scored since Week 1, but will in Week 4. 4. Jets RB Braelon Allen (+115) I was a fan of Braelon Allen in the 2024 draft process because he's big at 6-foot-1, 235 pounds, and was the youngest player in the entire class. He actually racked up 482 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns as a rookie, but an injury held him to four games played last year. Now, he's making his third career start with Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury. When the New York Jets get in the red zone against the Chicago Bears , Frank Reich is going to call his number. 5. Saints RB Alvin Kamara (+135) (Monday) This game is on Monday night, but I had to mention it. The Saints are hosting the Atlanta Falcons in the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth Game," where the Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina. The legendary Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the opening drive of the game, which set the tone for an emotional 23-3 Saints victory. I can't imagine what the environment will be like on Monday night. Travis Etienne is out with a hamstring injury, opening the door for franchise legend Alvin Kamara . He's not as productive as he used to be, but it makes too much sense for him to score in this game. Bonus: Ravens RB Derrick Henry 2 TDs (+250) Derrick Henry faces the team that selected him No. 45 overall in the 2016 NFL Draft this Sunday. Henry and the Titans didn't have some dramatic breakup, but Henry wanted to win football games and the Titans were about to suffer an embarrassing fall to the bottom of the league, so a mutual parting of ways made sense. It used to be a debate if Henry was a future Hall of Famer. Not anymore. The ageless wonder leads the NFL with 3,817 rushing yards and 38 rushing touchdowns since signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Those are more rushing yards and more rushing touchdowns than the entire Titans offense since he left. Derrick Henry to find the end zone at -210 is probably a parlay leg, but what about two touchdowns at +250? He's averaging two touchdowns a game this year as it is! However, the Rams, with two Ls, might be slightly more desperate than Philadelphia. And then over in the AFC, we've got Patrick Mahomes playing like he's back to his old form and Kirk Cousins lighting up the scoreboard. Let's dive into how I'm wagering on the weekend. Rams @ Eagles Simply put, I don’t think the Eagles are very good right now, and it might not be their year. I did not like the hiring of a first-time offensive coordinator to pair with Jalen Hurts and the results so far are on par with what I expected — a disjointed offense that ranks 17th in offensive DVOA. Hurts is ranked 27th in EPA per play. The Eagles' offensive line hasn’t been its usual self and I think the play-calling hasn’t made much sense. The Rams' defense is fourth in DVOA this season and should be able to disrupt the Eagles' offense in a meaningful way this Sunday. On the other side is an L.A. offense that has shown brilliant moments this season, while also displaying some weaknesses. Last week against the Broncos, the Rams started fast on offense and then disappeared, punctuated by a Matthew Stafford pick-six. Matthew Stafford will try to lead the Rams over the Eagles in NFL Week 4. (Getty Images) The possible return of Puka Nacua will help the Rams' passing attack. On paper, the Rams' offensive line should struggle in this game, but the Eagles' defensive line has been underwhelming. PFF has the Eagles' pass rush ranked 27th in the NFL and the tackling is ranked at about that level, too. The Rams are 1-2, and after blowing that game on Sunday, they need to win this weekend. You shouldn’t just solely wager on teams because they need to win, but that’s part of the equation for me. I get a better quarterback and a better coach who’s playing better football. Schwartz's Pick: Rams -3 Chiefs @ Raiders The Chiefs are 3-0 and playing better football on offense than they have in years. Mahomes looks completely healthy after missing the end of the season with an ACL injury. It was assumed Mahomes would be less mobile, but he’s been moving around the pocket and down the field like usual. In the Chiefs' first game against an excellent Broncos defense, he rushed for 23 yards. In Week 2 against the Colts, he rushed for 17 yards in an overtime win. Patrick Mahomes seems to have found his groove again. (Getty Images) Last week, Mahomes only rush attempt was when he kneeled. The Chiefs' offensive line has played fine this season, but the pass protection has been a concern. Now this group has to play Maxx Crosby and that’s a recipe for pressure on Mahomes. When Mahomes feels pressure or understands it might be a game featuring pressure, he tends to run the ball more often. Kansas City might also need to keep up with the Raiders' scoring output if Cousins continues to put up points for the Raiders. That will lead to a more aggressive Mahomes rushing the football. Here's where I'm putting my money. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. Our panel will use the same format as last year, sharing all their picks and challenging each other with opposing views on every game unless there's a unanimous selection. We'll also keep track of lone-wolf picks, which were 32-29-1 last year. Now, let's look ahead to the Week 1 slate, which starts Wednesday with the Super Bowl LX rematch and a lone-wolf pick right off the top. Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Sept. 9, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings . New England Patriots at Seattle Seahawks 1 of 16 AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba FanDuel Line: Seahawks (-3.5) Knox: Seahawks (-3.5) I don't think the Super Bowl LX rematch will be as one-sided as last year's championship game. However, I do believe Seattle's defensive front can prevent Drake Maye and the Patriots from finding an offensive rhythm once again. With home-field advantage playing a factor, Seattle should win by more than a field goal and walk away with a 1-0 record. Moton: Patriots (+3.5) It's understandable that the panel leaned heavily toward the Seahawks, given Seattle's dominant 29-13 victory over New England in Super Bowl LX seven months ago. Since then, the Seahawks have lost key parts of that team and coaching staff. Former Seahawks offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak is now the head coach of the Las Vegas Raiders. Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker, who led Seattle's backfield with 1,027 yards and five touchdowns, signed with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Seahawks also lost cornerback Riq Woolen and safety Coby Bryant in free agency. Meanwhile, the Patriots added wideouts A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Running back TreVeyon Henderson won't play because of an ankle injury, though Rhamondre Stevenson has handled a workhorse role in the past. New England covers the 3.5-point spread. Predictions Patriots: Moton Seahawks: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams (in Australia) 2 of 16 AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford FanDuel Line: Rams (-3.5) Hanford: Rams (-3.5) There's no team entering the season with bigger hype than the Rams, and I'm buying it. While you could argue that their travel plans and a 49ers team that's probably more overlooked than it should be entering the season is a recipe for an upset, I think the Rams will show right away why they're the Super Bowl favorites. L.A. wins by a touchdown behind a dominant defensive performance. O'Donnell: 49ers (+3.5) Both teams have been major offseason headline generators: the Rams for building a super team headlined by the Myles Garrett trade and return of Aaron Donald; and the 49ers for what boils down to a lot of negativity headlined by injuries. In fact, while almost all the focus has been on George Kittle's potential return in Week 1, we don't actually know if Christian McCaffrey will be fit to play, and conventional wisdom would be to back the favorites. But these two teams traveled a long, long way to play a football game, and I'd rather take the points against a familiar foe in an unfamiliar setting regardless of who is on the field. Predictions 49ers: Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Rams: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans 3 of 16 AP Photo/David J. Phillip Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud FanDuel Line: Bills (-1.5) Davenport: Bills (-1.5) Laying points on the road against arguably the NFL's best defense is starting the season with some anxiety. But I have that much more anxiety about C.J. Stroud after how he finished last season—Josh Allen leads the Bills to a close win on one of Week 1's better games. Gagnon: Texans (+1.5) Week 1 is a lot of gut, and I have a feeling the Houston defense will be extremely prepared for Buffalo in the Texans' home opener. That was certainly the case when they beat the Bills at this very site in November 2025. The Bills are an excellent team, but this is a tough spot for their new coach. Predictions Bills: Davenport Texans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski TOP NEWS New NFL Power Rankings 📊 Bleacher Report 9h Viral Rams Coach Vid 🖕 Bleacher Report 4h Injury-stricken Seahawks signing veteran RB Bleacher Report 5h Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers 4 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams FanDuel Line: Bears (-2.5) Moton: Bears (-2.5) The Bears enter this matchup with a shaky secondary. Safety Coby Bryant underwent knee surgery and will miss a few months of action. Slot cornerback Kyler Gordon is on the physically unable to perform list with a calf injury. However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young hasn't shown the ability to exploit opposing pass defenses' weaknesses, averaging just 180.2 passing yards per game over his three-year career. Bears go on the road with their ascending offense and win by at least a field goal. Sobleski: Bears (-2.5) The Carolina Panthers finished among the bottom six in total offense last season. The organization added next-to-nothing to improve the unit. If anything, the group might be worse since both offensive tackle spots remain a serious concern. Conversely, the Chicago Bears are explosive enough offensively to easily cover this spread. Predictions Bears: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars 5 of 16 AP Photo/Gary McCullough Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence FanDuel Line: Jaguars (-7.5) Gagnon: Jaguars (-7.5) I think the Browns could have some surprisingly nice moments this season, but this ain't the spot. Cleveland is, at the very least, a work in progress as a new core and coaching staff settle in. The Jaguars, on the other hand, are a well-oiled machine on a strong trajectory following a superb second half to the 2025 campaign. I expect them to keep rolling in their home opener. Sobleski: Browns (+7.5) Despite every expectation of the Cleveland Browns' offense imploding thanks to questionable quarterback setup, Todd Monken's squad gets the benefit of the doubt in the head coach's debut because of its defense. Myles Garrett might be gone, but this unit still has playmakers at all three levels to slow the Jaguars and make the contest interesting. Predictions Browns: Hanford, Knox, Sobleski Jaguars: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, O'Donnell Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers 6 of 16 AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers FanDuel Line: Steelers (-3.5) Gagnon: Falcons (+3.5) I don't trust the Steelers, and I hate that hook for them. It's really that simple. These teams are closer to being evenly matched than many might believe, and the Steelers were far from impressive at home in 2025. The Falcons didn't lose by more than a field goal in regulation in any of their last six road games last season. They should keep this game tight. Hanford: Steelers (-3.5) The jury is out on Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy's reunion in Pittsburgh and the impact it will have on a stagnant Steelers offense, but I just don't see the "winner" of the NFL's least inspiring QB battle, Tua Tagovailoa, doing serious damage to the Steelers defense. I expect this game to be ugly, like most Steelers games, but Tagovailoa makes one too many mistakes as Pittsburgh improves to 6-1 ATS in its last seven games against Atlanta. Predictions Falcons: Gagnon Steelers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New York Jets at Tennessee Titans 7 of 16 AP Photo/George Walker IV Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward FanDuel Line: Titans (-1.5) Davenport: Jets (+1.5) Fans who watch this entire game should receive some sort of reparations from the NFL. Neither offense in this slopfest can be trusted even a little, but for my money the Jets are slightly better defensively. First team to 13 points wins! Knox: Titans (-1.5) I'm inclined to believe it when I see it with Robert Saleh, Cam Ward, and the Titans. However, I believe they at least have the potential to turn things around quickly. The Jets? Not so much. I believe that New York is playing for 2027 and beyond. I don't envision Tennessee running away with this one, but I don't see the Jets winning on the road, and this is awfully close to a pick'em. Predictions Jets: Davenport Titans: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions 8 of 16 AP Photo/Caroline Brehman New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough FanDuel Line: Lions (-7) Hanford: Saints (+7) The Saints closed last season red hot, and while some of that may be fool's gold, I think they'll keep this one within a touchdown. I expect Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Co. to have success against the Saints' defense, but I don't trust the Lions' secondary to give Tyler Shough major issues. Lions win by six in a high-scoring game. O'Donnell: Lions (-7) Hey, the Saints are going to be feisty, and the panel is just about split on the Lions giving this many points for good reason. Missing the playoffs a year ago should be gnawing at Dan Campbell's group, though. Detroit scored an average of 32-plus points per game at home last season — a full touchdown more than on the road. Can the Saints go toe-to-toe in a shootout with the Lions in Detroit? Maybe, but I'll back a first-week barrage from the stronger offensive unit as the Lions look to set the tone for a rebound campaign. Predictions Saints: Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Lions: Davenport, Gagnon, O'Donnell Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals 9 of 16 AP Photo/Carolyn Kaster Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow FanDuel Line: Bengals (-3.5) Knox: Buccaneers (+3.5) If Joe Burrow can stay healthy, Cincinnati's new-look defense should make the Bengals legitimate AFC contenders. However, the Bengals have been notorious for slow starts under Zac Taylor. I can't envision them winning big against a Buccaneers team that can play the underdog card after missing the playoffs in 2025. Sobleski: Bengals (-3.5) Joe Burrow and Co. should hit the ground running. Can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers do the same without Mike Evans on the roster? Obviously, quarterback Baker Mayfield has other weapons in Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan. However, the Cincinnati Bengals still have an advantage in offensive firepower with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who were both back at practice this week. Predictions Buccaneers: Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell Bengals: Davenport, Gagnon, Moton, Sobleski Baltimore Ravens at Indianapolis Colts 10 of 16 AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson FanDuel Line: Ravens (-3.5) Hanford: Ravens (-3.5) Backing this many favorites at 3.5 makes me antsy, but I think the Ravens will be too much for the Colts here. I'm not sold on the Ravens overall this season, but I think their improved defense under Jesse Minter, with the addition of Trey Hendrickson, should give them enough punch to make life very difficult for Daniel Jones. Lamar Jackson has to get back on track as a passer this season, but I think he makes enough plays to put Baltimore over the top. Sobleski: Colts (+3.5) Interestingly, the Indianapolis Colts' defense has a very specific matchup in its favor, with the defensive tackle duo of DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart facing two brand-new starters along the Baltimore Ravens' offensive line. Thus, the Colts could control the line of scrimmage to make life difficult on quarterback Lamar Jackson and running back Derrick Henry. Offensively, Indianapolis should have all of its pieces back in place to get off to a hot start, as it did last season. Predictions Ravens: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton Colts: Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles 11 of 16 AP Photo/Daniel Kucin Jr. Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels FanDuel Line: Eagles (-5.5) Hanford: Eagles (-5.5) The Eagles have a lot of questions to answer on the offensive side of the ball in Week 1, but I'm just not buying the Commanders yet. Jayden Daniels is healthy, which will help, but the weapons around him leave some to be desired, and the absence of star LT Laremy Tunsil will loom large against an Eagles defense that loves to get after the quarterback. I'm not sure Jalen Hurts silences the critics in Week 1, but I do think the Eagles have enough juice in the run game and on defense to control the game and win by a touchdown. Moton: Commanders (+5.5) This is a divisional matchup, and both quarterbacks are learning new offenses. Expect both teams to be inefficient in a game of missed opportunities, while both defenses capitalize on miscues with takeaways. Philadelphia also lost some offensive explosiveness when it traded three-time Pro Bowl receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. On the ground, running back Saquon Barkley helps the Eagles grind out a close victory by a margin short of a touchdown. Predictions Commanders: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Eagles: Davenport, Hanford Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings 12 of 16 AP Photo/Abbie Parr Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson FanDuel Line: Vikings (-1.5) Davenport: Packers (+1.5) Neither of these teams are especially easy to trust in the early-going this year—the Vikings have a new quarterback in Kyler Murray and the Packers have significant questions on defense, especially where the pass rush is concerned. I'll take the points—with exactly zero confidence. Gagnon: Vikings (-1.5) I don't know how I feel about the Packers opening the season on the road against a sneaky-good division rival without Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons. Throw in the unpredictability factor with Kyler Murray, and I think Green Bay is in a tough situation here. Predictions Packers: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell Vikings: Davenport, Sobleski Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders 13 of 16 AP Photo/John Locher Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty FanDuel Line: Raiders (-3.5) Moton: Raiders (-3.5) According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Las Vegas Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers is expected to miss "a game or two" after undergoing a trim on his meniscus. On a positive note from the injury front, head coach Klint Kubiak is optimistic about running back Ashton Jeanty suiting up after he suffered an ankle injury during practice on August 23. Without Bowers, expect the Raiders to feature Jeanty (if healthy) and rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. on the ground, which should be enough to control time of possession. The Miami Dolphins offense may not see much time on the field. Although the Raiders have an unproven secondary, with rookie second-rounder Treydan Stukes likely to play at safety and second-year pro Darien Porter at the No. 2 cornerback spot, quarterback Kirk Cousins is more equipped to dice up a shaky pass defense than Malik Willis. O'Donnell: Dolphins (+3.5) Woof. Two organizations in complete rebuild mode. Two new starting quarterbacks under new coaching staffs. Just give me the points in this one, and I'll figure out what to do with these two for the rest of the season after Week 1. Predictions Dolphins: Hanford, O'Donnell Raiders: Davenport, Gagnon, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers 14 of 16 AP Photo/Gregory Bull Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert FanDuel Line: Chargers (-9.5) Davenport: Cardinals (+9.5) To be clear, the Arizona Cardinals have about as much chance of winning this game as I do of winning an Academy Award. But Arizona has talent on offense and showed it can move the ball last season—Jacoby Brissett will lead a garbage-time touchdown drive late and the Redbirds will sneak in the back door for the cover. Moton: Chargers (-9.5) Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been teammates with his top pass-catchers for multiple years, and the team added tight end David Njoku, who has 384 receptions for 4,062 yards and 34 touchdowns in his nine-year career. With newly established offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel calling the plays, the Chargers could score in flurries against the Cardinals, who retained defensive coordinator Nick Rallis after his unit gave up the fourth-most points last season. Predictions Cardinals: Davenport, Hanford Chargers: Gagnon, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants 15 of 16 AP Photo/Rick Scuteri Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott FanDuel Line: Cowboys (-2.5) Knox: Cowboys (-2.5) Will the Giants be better under new head coach John Harbaugh? Yes. Are they prepared to keep pace with a team that has one of the NFL's top offenses and a vastly improved defense? At this point in the season, I don't believe so. Week 1 divisional matchups can be unpredictable, and I won't be shocked if the Giants steal this one. I think it's far more likely that Dallas makes one or two defensive plays that it wouldn't have made a year ago to preserve a one-score victory. O'Donnell: Giants (+2.5) The Cowboys are the better team on paper, and the Giants' secondary will have a hard time defending CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens even if Big Blue is getting to Dak Prescott. But if a new coaching staff and the return of two injured star players to the lineup (Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers), on top of two rookie first-round picks starting in their debuts (Arvell Reese and Francis Mauigoa), at home on Sunday Night Football against a bitter rival, isn't enough to get a team up, then what in the gorydamn hell are we playing this game for? Predictions Cowboys: Davenport, Knox, Moton, Sobleski Giants: Gagnon, Hanford, O'Donnell Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs 16 of 16 AP Photo/Jack Dempsey Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix FanDuel Line: Chiefs (-2.5) Knox: Broncos (+2.5) Winning as the road team in Kansas City is tough, but defense travels, and the Broncos have one of the best in the business. Beyond that, I think it's going to take a few games for Patrick Mahomes to find his groove with whatever post-injury playing style he brings to the 2026 season. The Chiefs will go as Mahomes does, and one or two instances of him hesitating behind the line will sink them against arguably the most well-rounded team in the conference. O'Donnell: Chiefs (-2.5) The Denver defense is going to be a problem for Kansas City, especially with a less than 100% healthy Patrick Mahomes back under center. On paper, the Broncos might be the better all-around team, too. And the Chiefs have lost two of the last three season openers, with the lone victory being a controversial end-of-game call that gave K.C. the victory over Baltimore in 2024. Yeah, all things point to a Broncos cover, if not an outright win. So, I'll ride with the minority and lay these points with the home team covering late. Without further ado, here are three of the best player props for NFL Week 1, including Garrett Wilson, David Montgomery and Omarion Hampton. *]:mx-auto lg:[&>*]:mx-0"> Best NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Week 1 David Montgomery Anytime TD (-120) David Montgomery has found a new home in Houston. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season. They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players. He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. Smith might have turnover issues, but he is not afraid to let it fly. Since the start of the 2022 season, he ranks fourth in the NFL in pass attempts. This Titans defense is very vulnerable, and Frank Reich should let Geno Smith chuck it early and often in this game. Last season, the Titans ranked 29th in the NFL in defensive EPA/pass and 26th in dropback success rate. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. Omarion Hampton Over 68.5 Rushing Yards (-114) This should be a big season for Omarion Hampton. He only played nine games in his rookie season for the Chargers, but he is set for a huge role in what should be a productive Los Angeles offense. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. That defense has a lot of young, inexperienced pieces and should struggle again this season. The Chargers should feed the ball to Hampton early and often to control the game against Arizona. The Chargers are also big favorites and should lead this game down the stretch. That should lead to a lot of carries for Hampton down the stretch while the Chargers put the game on ice. Tool Fantasy Cheat Sheet NFL Player Prop Odds FAQ What Are NFL Player Props? NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. We cover passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards, and anytime touchdowns in our tool, but there are countless other betting opportunities every week. Every prop bet has two parts: The number (Over or Under 81.5 rushing yards, for example) The price, which determines how much a winning bet returns and reflects the implied probability If two players are lined at 45.5 receiving yards, that does not necessarily mean they have the same implied odds. Now, the star faces a Titans team that allowed 142 yards on 32 carries against the Jets duo of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen. In that game, Tennessee’s Rush EPA/Play Allowed was -0.038, which was right around the -0.043 mark the team posted in 2025. All offseason long, we talked about Robert Saleh shaping up this defense, but there is a chance he won’t be successful in doing so. That said, this might just be a strong matchup for an elite rusher. Barkley is averaging 96.9 rushing yards per game in his last 30 games, and he has rushed for at least 78 yards in five of his last six games. Also, since signing with the Eagles, Barkley is averaging 100.4 rushing yards per game when Philly is favored by between 5.5 and 8 points. I just don’t see any reason he can’t get going in this game, and I’ll throw out the fact that the game script could really favor him. If the Eagles go up early, they’ll begin to rely on the run. Bet: Saquon Barkley Over 75.5 Rushing Yards (-135) & Alt Rushing Yards 100+ (+233 – 0.25 units) Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears – 1:00 pm ET I tweeted during last week’s game that I can’t understand how Wentz is the backup over JJ McCarthy, but that’s neither here nor there. Wentz went on to do just fine in a win over the Packers, and I don’t see the Vikings being shy about throwing the ball here. With the Bears having put 59 points on the Panthers, there’s just no way of standing a chance against them without making plays in the passing game. And if Bryce Young can go for 361 passing yards against this defense, you’d think Wentz can reach 225 with all of the weapons he has at his disposal. Also, the absence of Jordan Mason only makes it more likely that Kevin O’Connell will let Wentz cook — even if he’s doing it with a microwave. Wentz only threw for 133 yards in relief of an injured Kyler Murray lat week, but he also threw for at least 236 yards in three of his final four appearances in 2025. Two of those three games featured him throwing for over 300 yards. I’m not sure the result of this game will be pretty for Minnesota, but I see Wentz putting up a pretty decent yardage total. I actually really wanted to get more aggressive with this, but the pricing wasn’t great. Also, the Broncos had a better offseason than the Jaguars. So, while things did look ugly offensively last week, I’m chalking it up to a weird game. I don’t think anyone should be sounding the alarms on Davis Webb running the offense, and I feel good about Denver bouncing back at home. Under Sean Payton, the Broncos are 4-1 both straight-up and against the spread in home games with totals of 45.5 or higher. Denver also happens to be 6-1 both SU and ATS after scoring 14 or fewer points in its previous game. Those trends support a much better performance from the Broncos — and especially the Denver offense — in Week 2. It’s also pretty easy to envision the Broncos corners enjoying a matchup with an average group of receivers. Denver can also put some pressure on Trevor Lawrence, and I trust the defense to do well against a shaky Jacksonville backfield. On top of all of that, the Broncos look rather sharp here. The point is to bet props where the price is in your favor often enough to matter across a season. What are NFL player props? An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Instead of betting on the winner, point spread, or total score, you're betting on a specific outcome or statistic for that player. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Receptions and receiving yards (wide receivers, tight ends, and running backs). Anytime, first, and multiple touchdown scorers (eligible offensive players and defenses/special teams). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. You can bet the over if you think he'll finish with 246 or more, or the under if you think he'll finish with 245 or fewer. Touchdown scorer props work differently: you’re simply betting whether a player scores, with the odds reflecting the sportsbook's assessment of how likely that is. One thing that makes player props different from game bets is how much they depend on the game script. A team that falls behind by three scores is likely to throw more and run less, which can boost passing and receiving opportunities while cutting into rushing volume. That's why our projections account for the expected game script when estimating how a player is likely to perform. Player and game context : The projections consider player usage, recent and historical performance, injuries and availability, opponent strength, coaching tendencies, and the expected game environment. We also incorporate advanced metrics and play-by-play data. From projection to probability : We run simulations of the upcoming game to estimate how often a player finishes over or under the specific line being offered. That gives us the probability shown on the board. Probability meets price : We compare our projected probability with the probability implied by the sportsbook's odds.
